value: ChatGPT (LLM-based conversational system). Most studies were prompt experiments with standardized text inputs submitted to ChatGPT; some involved real participants interacting with ChatGPT. Delivery is primarily text-based, with one study using multimodal input (speech rhythm and rate). Interaction is asynchronous. Studies used standard ChatGPT (n=50), custom instruction GPT (n=4), and customized GPT (n=6).
quotes:
“ChatGPT, a conversational system based on the large language model (LLM) GPT, developed by OpenAI, that processes and analyzes large amounts of data to generate responses to user inquiries.”
“Most studies were designed as prompt experiments (n=50), in which the accuracy or the quality of ChatGPT-generated responses to various queries were evaluated, without involvement of human participants”
“a study showed that providing multimodal input, namely speech rhythm and rate, besides text-based data, increased ChatGPT's accuracy in distinguishing between anxiety and depression”
loc: Introduction; Results, Characteristics of Clinical Applications, p.4-5; Discussion, Factors Accounting for Performance Variability, p.8
age_as_reported: adults (n=56), children and adolescents (n=4)

title: Exploration of Mental Health and Stress Among Nursing Interns Through a Chatbot: A Single-Group Pilot Study.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: Chatbot delivered via LINE messaging platform; text-based exchanges; asynchronous interaction with automated responses and real-time guidance
quotes:
“Chatbots are conversational agents designed to interact with users through natural language, primarily via text-based exchanges in messaging applications”
“The LINE messaging platform was used to deliver the X-LAC intervention”
age_as_reported: third-year daytime nursing students with mean age of 21.6 years (SD = 1.05)

title: Artificial intelligence in the psychologist's toolkit: Psypilot as a case study.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: AI-powered clinical assistance platform (copilot for psychologists); uses LLM with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG); clinician-facing decision support tool, not a patient-facing chatbot; web-based platform with text interaction
quotes:
“Psypilot is an AI-powered clinical assistance platform designed specifically for psychologists and mental health services”
“Psypilot augments model context using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)”

title: Designing conversational intelligence: effect of large language models (GPT-driven) platforms for precision maternal and newborn health engagement: a systematic review.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: Multiple modalities across 15 included studies: LLM/GPT chatbots (text-based), NLP-based chatbots integrated into Android apps, SMS and email outreach, web app-based chatbots, Telegram-based chatbot. Primary delivery format is text. Some chatbots integrate video, images/avatars, and voice/audio functionalities. Interaction is primarily asynchronous via text messaging, with some real-time query resolution.
quotes:
“LLM/GPT-powered conversational agents”
“Text-based (SMS and email)”
“Text-based chatbot, operational via Telegram app”
“Text-based (web app)”
“The type of data generated by LLM/GPTs in the context of these sources is primarily text.”
“Two LLM/GPT chatbots for postpartum and newborn care using SMS and email outreach.”
country: Multi-country (12 countries across included studies; review conducted from Iran)
age_as_reported: Pregnant and postpartum women (and partners); one study included women aged 18–40

title: The Digital Therapeutic Alliance With Mental Health Chatbots: Diary Study and Thematic Analysis.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: Mobile app chatbots (Woebot and Wysa) with text-based delivery and asynchronous interaction. Both operated mainly with predefined decision pathways and natural-language classifiers rather than open-ended generative AI. Woebot uses structured responses with predefined reply options (closed-ended); Wysa offers free-text input with fewer prompts allowing open-ended conversations.
quotes:
“At the time of this study, both Woebot and Wysa operated mainly with predefined decision pathways and natural-language classifiers, rather than open-ended generative AI”
“Wysa offers a free-text input field with fewer prompts, allowing for open-ended conversations. Woebot, on the other hand, relies on structured responses, requiring users to select from preset options”
age_as_reported: aged 17 to 35 years (mean age 23, SD 4.66 y)

title: Empowering pediatric, adolescent, and young adult patients with cancer utilizing generative AI chatbots to reduce psychological burden and enhance treatment engagement: a pilot study.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: Generative AI chatbot (LLM-based, GPT-4) delivered via smartphone messaging application (LINE platform). Text-based, asynchronous interaction. Two age-specific chatbot models (Model A for elementary/junior high; Model B for high school and above).
quotes:
“Two age-appropriate AI chatbots, leveraging GPT-4, were developed to provide natural, empathetic conversations”
“The chatbots were integrated into a smartphone application using the LINE platform, Japan's widely adopted messaging service”
age_as_reported: pediatric and adolescent/young adult (AYA) cancer patients

title: Current Landscape and Future Directions for Mental Health Conversational Agents for Youth: Scoping Review.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: Chatbots (conversational agents) delivered via mobile apps (16/39, 41%), web applications (11/39, 28%), and desktop applications (6/39, 15%); some available on multiple channels (11/39, 28%). All supported text-based input (39/39, 100%); 2 studies (5%) also supported audio/speech input. All supported textual output (39/39, 100%); 64% supported multimedia output including images, video, audio, and games. Interaction was primarily synchronous text-based conversation.
quotes:
“Most CAs were delivered through mobile apps (16/39, 41%), followed by web applications (11/39, 28%) and desktop applications (6/39, 15%)”
“In all the reviewed studies (39/39, 100%), mental health CAs supported text as the primary mode of input. In 5% (2/39) of the studies, mental health CAs supported audio input along with textual input”
“All the CAs (39/39, 100%) supported text as the primary mode of output. In 64% (25/39) of the studies, it was indicated that CAs support multimedia outputs”
country: USA, NZL, AUS, GBR, CHN, BRA, DEU, ITA, NOR, ARG, BGD, BEL, CAN, NLD, PHL, PRT
age_as_reported: youth aged between 15 and 24 years (UN definition); included studies cover adolescents (12-18), young adults (18-30), and youth (14-25)

title: Conversational Agent Interventions for Mental Health Problems: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
label: Modality and delivery format
value: Four types of conversational agents (CAs): (1) chatbot - text or voice-based using artificial intelligence, (2) embodied conversational agent (ECA) - digital characters simulating verbal and nonverbal communication (speech, gestures, facial expressions), (3) CA in virtual reality (VR) - for controlled exposure in VR environments, (4) avatar - used in avatar therapy. Delivery includes text, voice, and multimodal formats.
quotes:
“Interventions with four types of CAs were eligible: (1) chatbot, a software program that simulates conversations with users through text or voice depending on artificial intelligence”
“(2) embodied CA (ECA), the digital characters that simulate key properties of human face-to-face conversation, both verbal and nonverbal (eg, speech, gestures, and facial expressions)”
“(3) CA in virtual reality (VR), which offers a safe, convenient, and accessible medium to the controlled exposure to anxiety-inducing stimuli within a VR environment”
“(4) avatar, referring to the CA in avatar therapy”
country: USA, GBR, SWE, JPN, KOR, CHE, CAN, ARG, CHN, IRL, NLD, DEU, NZL
age_as_reported: The average age was 36.32 (SD 13.44; range 21.40-71.47) years

title: RACares: a conceptual design to guide mHealth relational agent development based on a systematic review.

quotes:

“they use natural language to communicate with users, provide support, and personalize interactions to meet individual needs”
“RAs can also provide support in a variety of formats, including text-based messaging, voice assistants, and virtual reality environments”

title: Essays on digital technology-enabled mental healthcare delivery.
label: Modality and delivery format
value: The thesis covers three interventions: (1) A mental health mobile app (MHMA) called 'Hope' for iOS/Android offering self-reflection and anonymous online community functions (text-based, asynchronous). (2) An AI-enabled online mental health service referral platform delivering personalized referrals through a text-based chatbot. (3) Telemental health services (telemedicine via videoconferencing). The chatbot facilitates text-based conversations; the MHMA is app-based with text posts and survey responses.
quotes:
“Hope is a free platform available for iOS or Android smartphone users. It offers two distinct functions for self-support and peer-support purposes”
“deliver the personalized referral process through a chatbot”
“The chatbot is an AI-powered bot which facilitates text-based conversations with the users.”
age_as_reported: Not explicitly stated as an age band for the overall thesis; Essay 1 sample mean age ~23.5 years; Essay 2 target users described as 'young adults'; Essay 3 uses population-level data

title: Artificial intelligence in perinatal mental health research: A scoping review.

Text and audio delivery. Synchronous interaction for chatbots/voice assistants.
quotes:
“Perinatal mood change examination through SMS or Facebook messenger supported by AI chatbot.”
“The voice assistants tested included Apple Siri, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, and Microsoft Cortana, all installed on mobile devices.”
“Supervised machine learning chatbot”

quotes:

“The chatbot was designed to engage users in conversation, guiding through mindfulness exercises, providing information about mindfulness and offering personalised feedback.”

“The app is powered by Google Commerce Limited and was downloaded in version 9.1.2, with text-based chat functionalities only”

quotes:
“Initial feedback on the chatbot and survey was gathered through an internal testing within the research team, involving 15 participants.”
“The application was then provided to counselors at the partner university for further testing and feedback, with 6 counselors testing the app.”

“we scraped 100 Reddit posts from mental health subreddits and used them to simulate user queries. This process revealed 2 main issues: some chatbot responses contained gibberish text, while others hinted at diagnostic language.”

Two pediatric psychosomatic physicians performed detailed review for emotional sensitivity and contextual accuracy. Attending physicians of participating patients reviewed final models for safety before deployment. Multiple LLMs tested (GPT-4, Gemini Ultra, Claude 3 Opus); GPT-4 selected. No patient co-design reported.

title: Current Landscape and Future Directions for Mental Health Conversational Agents for Youth: Scoping Review.
label: Session dose, duration and structure
value: Duration of CA interaction ranged from a single session (6/39, 15%) to <4 weeks (12/39, 31%), 4-8 weeks (5/39, 13%), and 9-16 weeks (1/39, 3%). Content delivery was flexible (25/39, 64%), structured (8/39, 20%), or semistructured (3/39, 8%). Structured models delivered prewritten content via rule-based programming for a predefined period (days to weeks). Flexible models allowed users to choose content or navigate based on input. Semistructured models combined core psychological concepts for all users with user-specified preferences.

title: A Mental Health Chatbot with Cognitive Skills for Personalised Behavioural Activation and Remote Health Monitoring.
label: Session dose, duration and structure
value: Repeated/multi-session intervention. Each interaction follows a 10-step process: (1) Feelings check; (2) Recap previous session/review homework; (3) Agree on an agenda; (4) Check for any unexpected/unplanned activities or incidents; (5) Get out clause; (6) Do the work; (7) Summarise what was discussed; (8) Set homework; (9) Schedule next meeting; (10) Feelings check. Pilot study period was 8 weeks. On average, users scheduled three activities per week and engaged in conversation seven times during the study period. PHQ2/PHQ9 questionnaires need to be performed with a two-week gap; mood score can be recorded each time the user participates in an activity or uses the app.

“Bunji follows a 10-step process each time a user interacts with the app. A feelings check is conducted as the first step.”
“The PHQ2/PHQ9 questionnaires need to be performed with a two-week gap, but the mood score can be recorded each time the user participates in an activity or uses the app.”
“On average, users scheduled three activities per week. On average, a user engaged in a conversation with Bunji seven times during the study period.”
