value: Workflow-orchestrated using basic expert systems framework with conditional rules from knowledge base. Hierarchical decision tree structure with menu-based dialogue. Deterministic components with strict conditional rules to reduce risk in mental health use case.
quotes:
“The chatbot was developed using a basic expert systems framework; a type of artificial intelligence that responds to user input by combining the user's previous responses with conditional rules from a knowledge base”
“The chat flow followed a hierarchical decision tree, with inputs from the user sourced via a menu-based dialogue”
“stricter conditional rules reducing the likelihood of any unforeseen issues occurring in an AI system with greater autonomy”
age_as_reported: Age 31.23 (SD 4.09), range 24–39 (fathers); clinicians age 40.8 (SD 10.86), range 27–60

title: Clinical Efficacy, Therapeutic Mechanisms, and Implementation Features of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy-Based Chatbots for Depression and Anxiety: Narrative Review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Three architectures: (1) rule-based systems with preprogrammed scripts and decision trees (ensuring safety and consistency but limiting personalization); (2) hybrid models combining rule-based safeguards with NLP and machine learning classifiers (enabling greater flexibility while maintaining clinical oversight, e.g., Wysa, Youper); (3) generative models powered by large language models (producing open-ended responses and naturalistic dialogue, e.g., Therabot, Limbic Care) but requiring strict safeguards to mitigate risks of misinformation or hallucinated outputs.
quotes:
“Rule-based systems rely on preprogrammed scripts and decision trees, ensuring safety and consistency but limiting personalization. Hybrid models combine rule-based safeguards with natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning classifiers, enabling greater flexibility while maintaining clinical oversight”
“Generative models, powered by large language models, can produce open-ended responses and more naturalistic dialogue (eg, Therabot and Limbic Care) but require strict safeguards to mitigate risks of misinformation or hallucinated outputs.”
age_as_reported: Diverse populations including college/university students, postpartum women, adults with chronic conditions, adults with insomnia, subclinical/community young adults, paying app users, and adults with substance use problems

title: Feasibility and impact of a mental health chatbot on postpartum mental health: a randomized controlled trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture; uses natural language processing algorithms (Language Detection Protocol) to detect self-harm phrases in user free-text input, with deterministic safety responses. Content is pre-authored CBT/IPT-based psychoeducation and empathy delivered through conversational interactions.
quotes:
“Woebot's LDP uses natural language processing algorithms to detect and flag several hundred potential self-harm phrases (including some misspellings and slang phrases) with 98% accuracy”
“Upon detection and conﬁrmation of any concerning topics, LDP initiates a conversation between the chatbot Woebot and the participant to remind them of the application's limitations of services and offer a resource list”
age_as_reported: 18 years or above

title: Expert Consensus Best Practices for the Safe, Ethical, and Effective Design and Implementation of Artificially Intelligent Conversational Agent (i.e., Chatbot/Virtual Human) Systems in Health Care Applications.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Recommends human-in-the-loop approach with AI as supportive tool and human professionals as primary decision-makers. Mentions LLMs and NLP as generative components. Content constraints include evidence-based source validation, guardrails for crisis detection, and deferral to human professionals for clinical decisions.
quotes:
“The proposed model for safe and practical implementation is described as a "human-in-the-loop" approach to maintain the balance between AI assistance and human expertise.”
“the AICA should be designed to defer to professionals when needed to prevent users from developing a dependency on the AICA for diagnosis and treatment of serious health conditions.”

title: The development and use of chatbots in enhancing health care access for underserved and vulnerable populations: a scoping review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: 13 chatbots were rule-based (deterministic/predefined responses), 4 were hybrid combining rule-based and NLP, and 1 was exclusively NLP-based. The predominance of rule-based systems is attributed to greater reliability, compatibility with weak infrastructure, and lower error likelihood. NLP used complementarily for unpredictable scenarios and complex interactions.
quotes:
“13 were designed using rule-based systems. Four others operated as hybrid systems, leveraging both predefined rules and NLP, while only one chatbot was entirely NLP-based.”
“AI capabilities are typically employed as a complementary approach to manage unpredictable scenarios and more complex interactions.”
loc: Results, Chatbot design section, p.14; Discussion p.15-16
country: USA, BRA, IND, PER, LSO, PAK, ZAF, COD, JOR, NGA
age_as_reported: adolescents and young adults; women; young people aged 18-21; young women aged 18-28

title: A chatbot-delivered intervention for optimizing social media use and reducing perceived isolation among rural-living LGBTQ+ youth: Development, acceptability, usability, satisfaction, and utility.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Workflow-orchestrated rule-based chatbot; deterministic tree structure; content hosted on external platforms (Amazon Web Services, YouTube, private server)
quotes:
“REALbot is a rule chatbot”
“Chat interactions followed a classic unidirectional "tree" structure”
“Infographics, videos, and stories with alternate endings were hosted in Amazon Web Services, YouTube, and a private server, respectively”
age_as_reported: 14–19 years of age (eligibility); ages 14–20 years old (participants)

title: AI-Enhanced Virtual Reality Self-Talk for Psychological Counseling: Formative Qualitative Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration. LLM (GPT-3.5) generates responses based on prompt and ongoing conversation. Deterministic elements: gaze activation, avatar switching, button-triggered transitions. Generative: LLM dialogue. Human operator interface available (MILO) allowing experimenter to select/modify text and decide when to intervene. Content constraints via prompt instructing motivational interviewer role, no AI disclosure. Guardrails: clinical psychologist present; system described as experimental.
quotes:
“Our LLM interface provides an interface for a human operator, which can be used by the experimenters”
“The operator can select parts of the text or even modify the text and send specific parts to the voice playback in the application.”
“We have also explored the possibility of allowing the experimenter to decide when to intervene in the conversation.”
“Please do not mention that you are an artificial intelligence in your replies. Act as a real person.”
“To mitigate latency, the system can be used in a continuous mode; that is, the system is prompted to keep generating responses after each counselor utterance”
loc: Iterative Design, p.5; Materials and Equipment, p.6
age_as_reported: 19 to 26 years (mean 23.43, SD 2.21 years)

title: Artificial intelligence chatbots as a source of virtual social support: Implications for loneliness and anxiety management.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Workflow-orchestrated / deterministic rule-based approach. Built using Voiceflow with visual scripting. Responses strictly drawn from a pre-defined script to ensure internal validity. No generative/ML components used. An if/else condition criterion was set for the initial 'hello' gate.
quotes:
“we designed the chatbot using a rule-based approach, where the chatbot responses are strictly drawn from a pre-defined script, ensuring consistent responses across all conditions”
“In this study, we used Voiceflow, a service that enables the custom development of AI agents that either follow a rule-based approach or ML design using visual scripting.”
“An if/else condition criterion was set, such that participants would need to type "hello" to proceed to the main conversation.”
age_as_reported: 18 to 78 years (Mage = 44.56, SDage = 15.88)

title: Transforming healthcare with chatbots: Uses and applications-A scoping review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Heterogeneous architectures across included studies: rule-based (AIML), NLP-based, machine learning, knowledge graphs, and LLMs (GPT-4, Gemini discussed in narrative). Some use Rasa NLU. Deterministic and generative components both present across studies. No systematic description of model autonomy or guardrails.
quotes:
“An AI-powered mobile chatbot psychologist is introduced, utilizing Artificial Intelligence Markup Language (AIML) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)”
“The medical chatbot model based on knowledge graphs achieves 99% accuracy”
“NLP and machine learning are the most effective approaches for building chatbots.”
“modern large language models (LLMs) that are accessible to the wide public such as GPT-4 and Gemini”
loc: Table 2 (Omarov et al.; Bhuvanesh et al.; Anjum et al.); Discussion p.18
country: Multi-country (included studies span India, China, USA, Bahrain, Brazil, Egypt, Italy, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Morocco, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Republic of Ireland)
age_as_reported: Varies across included studies; includes adults over 18, university students, postpartum women, general populations

title: Human-ai collaborative journaling with pocket-mind: A dual-prompt framework for emotional exploration and goal attainment. [References].
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: GPT-4-based generative LLM with structured prompt engineering using Chain-of-Thought and LogiCoT principles; role-based design philosophy with model as 'empathetic mental health coach'; deterministic prompt structure guides generative responses with explicit guardrails including empathy-first responses and contradiction avoidance
quotes:
“we designed a GPT-4-based dual-prompt approach to personalize the journaling experience”
“Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompt design”
“Wrapping Prompt incorporates the core ideas of Logical Chain-of-Thought (LogiCoT)”
“we adopt a three-pronged prompt engineering strategy: (1) Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompt design, (2) Wrap-ping prompt construction guided by LogiCoT principles, and (3) a role-based design philosophy.”
“the model is guided to perceive itself as "an empathetic and approachable mental health coach,"”
age_as_reported: ages 19–34; average age 26.7 years (SD = 4.2)

title: Bridging the Skills Gap: Evaluating an AI-Assisted Provider Platform to Support Care Providers with Empathetic Delivery of Protocolized Therapy.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Knowledge-based conversational AI system with NLU (Rasa pipeline), dialog management (finite-state policy based on PST steps), clinical knowledge graph (CKG), and NLG (template-based response generation with retrieval). Retrieval-based, not generative. The system uses a ranked list of empathetic responses predicted by a separate model. Finite-state policy determines therapeutic response suggestions.
quotes:
“The core of the provider platform is a knowledge-based conversational AI system designed to guide a user in providing mental health support using natural language understanding (NLU), dialog management (DM), clinical knowledge graph (CKG), and natural language generation (NLG) components.”
“a finite-state policy based on the PST steps”
“Response retrieval has several benefits over generation including the safety and controllability of the responses.”
loc: Methods, System Description p.2-3; Introduction p.1

title: Usability Comparison Among Healthy Participants of an Anthropomorphic Digital Human and a Text-Based Chatbot as a Responder to Questions on Mental Health: randomized Controlled Trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: The digital human used Dialogflow (Google) for conversation logic, suggesting a rule-based/workflow-orchestrated architecture. The text-only chatbot was developed on the Itsalive.io platform. The study notes that LLMs were not available at the time of construction. Deterministic components were used; no generative components. An assessment of alignment between the two interfaces' algorithms was conducted.
quotes:
“The digital human was implemented using Dialogflow (Google) for conversation logic and connected to the UNEEQ platform for the human-avatar interface.”
“Large language models and application programming interface models were not available at the time this chatbot was constructed”
“An assessment was conducted to evaluate the alignment of the text-only and digital human algorithms.”
loc: Methods - Construction of the User Interface
age_as_reported: 18 years or older; age of participants ranged from 24 to 68 years

title: New Doc on the Block: Scoping Review of AI Systems Delivering Motivational Interviewing for Health Behavior Change
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Range from deterministic rule-based/scripted logic to generative LLM-based systems (GPT-2 XL, GPT-3.5, GPT-4). Some hybrid systems combine rule-based logic with NLP or ML. Generative components dynamically respond to user input. Only 2/15 studies explicitly discussed safety measures (expert review processes, content validation). Most (13/15) did not describe guardrails against hallucinations or inappropriate content.
quotes:
“Some systems use scripted logic to guide conversations, while others rely on advanced generative models such as GPT-4 to dynamically respond to user input.”
“Only a minority of the included studies (2/15, 13%) explicitly discussed safety measures related to LLM-generated content.”
“Herbert et al [6] and Kumar et al [5] noted expert review processes to ensure safety and alignment with clinical guidance.”
loc: Introduction, p.2; Results, Study Characteristics, p.4
country: USA (review conducted); included studies from GBR, USA, CAN, HKG, DEU, KOR, SGP, NLD
age_as_reported: Study populations ranged from general adult users to patients with specific conditions; ages ranged from 16 to 65 years; some studies recruited college students

title: Applications of Large Language Models in the Field of Suicide Prevention: Scoping Review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Most studies (35/43, 81%) used BERT or a fine-tuned BERT variant for contextual understanding/classification tasks. GPT models were used in 9/43 (21%) studies, primarily for generative applications. In 33/43 (77%) studies, LLMs were used for contextual language understanding (deterministic classification); 9/43 (21%) used generative capabilities. The review notes guardrails are needed: 'models of LLM use in crisis support contexts are most likely to be those that are driven by clinical oversight, with sufficient guardrails in place to trigger referrals when clinically indicated.'
quotes:
“Most of the studies (35/43, 81%) applied some derivation of Google's BERT.”
“In 33 (77%) of the 43 studies, the primary purpose of LLMs was contextual understanding of language, while 9 (21%) studies extended upon this by using the capacity of LLMs to generate natural language responses to prompts”
“models of LLM use in crisis support contexts are most likely to be those that are driven by clinical oversight, with sufficient guardrails in place to trigger referrals when clinically indicated”
loc: Results, Base LLMs Used, p.5-6; Discussion, Clinical Applications, p.10

title: An Overview of Chatbot-Based Mobile Mental Health Apps: Insights From App Description and User Reviews.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Three conversation flow types across apps: (1) Guided — only predefined responses, no open input (6/10 apps); (2) Semiguided — mostly predefined with some open input but bot cannot process sentiments in text (Woebot); (3) Open-ended — open input with bot recognizing and extracting information from user input (Wysa, Nuna, Elomia). Some chatbots use AI/ML for intelligent Q/A. Crisis detection via keyword matching (e.g., 'suicide') in early stages.
quotes:
“Guided conversation—only allows the users to communicate with the chatbot with predefined responses from the chatbot. It does not allow any form of open input from the users.”
“Semiguided conversation—mostly allows the users to communicate with the chatbot with predefined responses and sometimes allows open inputs from the users. However, the bot cannot recognize the open user inputs and extract any information from them.”
“Open-ended conversation—allows the users to communicate with the chatbot with predefined responses and open inputs from the users. The bot can recognize the open user inputs and extract information from them.”

title: Chatbot-Based Assessment of Employees' Mental Health: Design Process and Pilot Implementation.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Workflow-orchestrated, rule-based deterministic system with predefined decision trees mapping all possible user journeys. No generative or LLM components. Safety protocol triggered by risk indicators or keywords.
quotes:
“The checkup assessment is rule-based, with the next steps determined by user responses”
“decision trees were defined, and all possible user journeys were mapped and analyzed”
“the system used for output generation (responses to the user's input) is fixed (based on predefined decision trees), the conversation opportunities are currently limited”
“the conversation follows a safety protocol that includes referral to the care network or, if necessary, to emergency services”
loc: Methods, Chatbot Development and Testing, p.3-4; Discussion, Limitations, p.7
age_as_reported: aged between 25 and 44 years (55/77, 71%)

title: Artificial Intelligence for Management of Major Depression: Initial Design, Progress, and Research Plans.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration: LLM (generative) used for conversational intake only; dialogue management system (deterministic, topic network based) controls topic flow and constrains the LLM; advice system is analytical, non-generative using pre-set text based on LASSO regression predictions; human-in-the-loop monitoring planned for real-time oversight
quotes:
“In our design, the LLM does not "generate" advice used in the recommendation to the client using next-word probabilities, as is characteristic of LLMs. The recommendation is delivered through pre-set, non-generative text.”
“The fourth component is a dialogue management system that minimizes digressions in the LLM conversations, using a topic network statistically derived from the AI's own knowledgebase.”
“The sixth component is an existing analytical, non-generative module that provides and explains treatment advice.”
age_as_reported: Not specified — study focuses on adult patients with MDD; no age band stated

title: Current Landscape of Mental Health Conversational Agents From a Trauma-Informed Care Lens: Scoping Review. [Review]
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Across 28 MHCAs: 16 (57.1%) rule-based (deterministic), 1 (3.6%) fully generative AI, 9 (32.1%) hybrid (both rule-based and AI). 2 (7.1%) unclear. Design recommendations favoured predefined validated content over AI-generated responses for safety. One recommendation noted 'human-in-the-loop monitoring for worsening symptoms by clinicians.'
quotes:
“Sixteen (16/28, 57.1%) MHCAs used rule-based functionality for conversation logic, 1 (1/28, 3.6%) was fully generative AI, and 9 (9/28, 32.1%) incorporated both.”
“To ensure safety, use predefined validated content rather than artificial intelligence–generated responses [78].”
loc: Results — Overview of MHCA Interventions p.8; Textbox 2 p.16

title: Language adaptations of mental health interventions: User interaction comparisons with an AI-enabled conversational agent (Wysa) in English and Spanish.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: rule-based system with NLP/NLU/ML components. Every response is pre-written by clinicians. Content structured to align with classifications influencing conversational flow. For Spanish interactions, content is translated at the backend.
quotes:
“It uses a rule-based system where every response is pre-written by clinicians”
“The app uses natural language processing, natural language understanding, and machine learning to interpret the user's messages”
“Wysa focuses on comprehending user input through classifications, where content is structured to align with these classifications, influencing the conversational flow”
“In the case of Spanish interactions, content is translated at the backend”
country: ARG, CRI, ECU, MEX, PRI, URY, PER, COL, CHL, ESP

title: Chatbot-assisted therapy for patients with methamphetamine use disorder: a preliminary randomized controlled trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: deterministic components (scheduled reminders, video recordings, structured MBRP sessions, daily BSRS-5 questionnaire) combined with generative conversational elements using NLP and deep learning. Chatbot deployed on LINE platform. Electronic reporting system allowed researchers to view summaries of patient app activity.
quotes:
“natural language processing and deep learning were applied in the dialog system”
“The design integrated crucial features such as natural language processing and machine learning capabilities, which were harmoniously interfaced with the Line chatbot platform.”
“An electronic reporting system allowed the researchers to view summaries of their patients' app activity.”
age_as_reported: 18-65 years

title: "It's Not Only Attention We Need": Systematic Review of Large Language Models in Mental Health Care.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: The review identifies both deterministic (rule-based chatbots, BERT-based classification) and generative (autoregressive LLMs like GPT-4, LLaMa-2) components. Customization via prompting (zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot, CoT), fine-tuning on domain datasets, and RAG. Some studies used prompting strategies to establish guardrails. Model autonomy varies: LLMs exhibit 'agency' with a 'proactive role' in integrated care. Content constraints mentioned via prompting strategies for guardrails.
quotes:
“most studies primarily rely on prompting to control model output and to adapt the model to the given context and data”
“various prompting strategies were applied, including zero-shot [80], one-shot [107], few-shot [75], and CoT prompting [84]”
“only 2 studies relied on RAG to customize the LLM to domain-specific tasks”
“several studies explicitly mentioned the use of prompting strategies to establish guardrails”
“LLMs exhibit agency, which assigns them a proactive role in such an integrated care context”
loc: Results, L1 section, pp.7-9; Discussion, p.17
age_as_reported: Not restricted to a specific age band; review covers LLMs in mental health care broadly. Notes that most evaluations focused on younger populations or students.

title: Use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in psychiatry and mental health care: a systematic review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: The review distinguishes generative AI (transformer/diffusion models producing non-predefined output) from rule-based systems (selecting predetermined responses from decision trees). Generative components are non-deterministic. No details on model autonomy, content constraints, or guardrails are reported as design features.
quotes: “we deemed it necessary to narrow our definition of generative AI to only include content generated in a less deterministic/preestablished manner (e.g., as seen in transformer and diffusion models such as those empowering ChatGPT, DALL·E, Sora and their equivalents).”

title: A chatbot architecture for promoting youth resilience
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Rule-based (deterministic) dialog graph architecture with thousands of dialog nodes; uses Google Dialogflow for intent matching of user input. Visual authoring interface (CMS) creates directed graph structure with color-coded node types. Hybrid potential noted: authors discuss future integration of deep-learning-based dialog for rapport building and discovery while retaining crafted dialog for evidence-based activities. Content constraints include emergency escalation module for risk phrases.
quotes:
“Such a rule-based dialog graph contains thousands of dialog nodes.”
“uses Dialogflow for matching user input to intents.”
“whether the user had expressed distress and triggered the emergency escalation module during the prior engagement.”
“We believe there are possibilities in the medium-term including machine learning of dialog policy (e.g. sequencing activities) and use of deep-learnt dialog for rapport building and discovery while retaining crafted dialog for evidence-based activities.”
age_as_reported: adolescents (secondary school students) and undergraduate university students

title: Does the Digital Therapeutic Alliance Exist? Integrative Review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Both rule-based (deterministic) and generative AI components described. Rule-based systems noted as limiting while generative AI enables free-flow conversations. Generative AI refers to complex mathematical algorithms that learn from large data sets.
quotes:
“rule-based conversational agents often provided inadequate responses, frustrating users and reducing engagement.”
“free-flow conversations, which enhanced user experience through personalization”
“generative AI, which refers to complex mathematical algorithms that can learn from large data sets to produce text, audio, or visuals that resemble those of a human”
loc: Results, User Engagement, p.6; Results, Facilitators and Barriers, p.7; Introduction, p.2

title: "I don't know what you mean by 'I am anxious' ": A new method for evaluating conversational agent responses to standardized mental health inputs for anxiety and depression. [References].
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Chatbots rely on scripted/precomposed interaction models (deterministic). VAs rely on generic web search for most responses. Chatbots used precomposed responses 77% of the time vs VAs 27%. Chatbots support clarifying follow-up questions; VAs generally do not.
quotes:
“many specialized textual Chatbots currently rely on scripted interaction models”
“VAs are more reliant on generic search, making them more responsive to unexpected queries, but less able to offer detailed advice about specific medical queries”
“Chatbots exploited precomposed responses 77% time, significantly more often than VAs (27%)”

title: Artificial Intelligence for Mental Health Monitoring: A Solution for Digital Behavioral Health Care and Education-An Umbrella Review. [Review]
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Both rule-based (deterministic) and AI-driven (generative/ML) chatbot components described. Hybrid models combining AI-driven assessments with human oversight mentioned. Chatbots equipped to escalate serious concerns to human therapists when crisis signs detected. No detail on content constraints or guardrails beyond crisis escalation.
quotes:
“Chatbots (rule‐based and AI‐driven) with NLP, ML capabilities”
“several developers introduced hybrid models that combined AI‐driven assessments with human oversight, allowing mental health professionals to review and validate AI‐generated insights before initiating intervention”
“the chatbot was also equipped to escalate serious concerns to human therapists when signs of crisis were detected”
age_as_reported: individuals of all age groups, from children to older adults; adults, adolescents, and individuals with psychiatric, neurological, or stress-related conditions

title: Co-developing a Mental Health and Wellbeing Chatbot With and for Young People.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration: pre-scripted (deterministic) content combined with some machine learning for intent detection. Responses are both automatically assembled and hand-written. Keyword detection for common phrases; model trained for longer phrases.
quotes:
“The system is using both pre-scripted and some machine learning that allows it to interpret participant intent and then respond with an answer that is both automatically assembled and hand-written by the researchers, youths and the expert reference group.”
“The implementation for this was be as simple as keyword detection (e.g., hello, thanks, nice, great, swear words), and train a model to detect the longer phrases like how are you, who made you).”
age_as_reported: 15–17 years of age

title: Behavior Emotion Therapy System and You: Co-Design and Evaluation of a Mental Health Chatbot and Digital Human for Mild to Moderate Anxiety in Healthy Participants.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Deterministic, rule-based NLP system with dialog-tree architecture built on Dialogflow (Google) and Itsalive.io. Little or no machine learning capability. Content is pre-authored; responses are matched via keyword detection. 99% consistency between interfaces demonstrated.
quotes:
“The collected questions and responses were used as a foundation for training the language model and identifying keywords for the rules-based chatbot in Google's chatbot platform: DialogFlow.”
“rules-based neuro-linguistic programming (NLP) systems with little or no machine learning capability”
“To assess the performance of both chatbot versions, a test was conducted where both BETSY versions were asked the same question 100 times. In 99% of the cases, both chatbots provided identical responses.”
loc: Results Phase 2, p.7-8; Discussion, p.9; Phase 2, Dialog-Tree Development section

title: Chatbot-Delivered Cognitive Behavioral Therapy in Adolescents With Depression and Anxiety During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Feasibility and Acceptability Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture with proprietary neurolinguistic programming and artificial intelligence designing personalized program in real time; powered by natural language processing and machine learning; fully automated relational conversational agent; safety net protocol detects concerning language and provides crisis hotline
quotes:
“Powered by natural language processing and machine learning techniques”
“Using proprietary neurolinguistic programing and artificial intelligence, the platform designs a personalized program to meet the user's needs in real time”
“The safety net protocol detects concerning language, confirms it with the user, and provides a local suicide crisis hotline number as needed.”
age_as_reported: 13 to 17 years

title: A Clinical Quality-Assurance Panel for Patient-Facing Black-Box Large Language Models in Healthcare: Anchored Forced-Choice Drift Monitoring for Sensitive Communication.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Black-box LLM (ChatGPT 5.4) accessed via consumer interface with no control over model internals, decoding settings, temperature, or random seed; deterministic prompt template with generative model responses constrained to one-line JSON output; prompt family treated as part of measurement instrument
quotes:
“Local teams can observe input-output behavior but cannot inspect model internals, control decoding settings, or reliably detect silent version changes”
“The interface did not expose a stable build identifier beyond the product label, and temperature and random seed were not user-controllable.”
“Outputs were restricted to a one-line JSON object containing trial_id, choice, and confidence”

title: Barriers and Facilitators to the Use of Large Language Model-Based Conversational Agents in Mental Healthcare: A Systematic Review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Mixed architectures across studies. Includes fine-tuned models (Sharma: GPT-3 fine-tuned), retrieval-augmented generation (Wang J.: RAG prompting), purpose-built models (Therabot on LLaMA2), and general-purpose LLMs (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude 3). Guardrails present in some systems but documented as problematic (Collins: guardrails paradoxically harmful). Deterministic safety guardrails coexist with generative components.
quotes:
“Wang J. et al. [44] demonstrated that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prompting improved contextual understanding”
“GPT-3 fine-tuned”
“Collins et al. documented safety guardrails paradoxically harming users by terminating therapeutic conversations at critical moments”
“Therabot (LLaMA2)”
loc: Section 3.5.3, p.10; Table 1, pp.5-6; Section 3.4.1, p.8
country: USA, CHN, GBR, AUS, DEU, ISR, JPN, KOR, SAU, ESP, SWE

title: AI-Facilitated Cognitive Reappraisal via Socrates 2.0: Mixed Methods Feasibility Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Multi-AI agent framework with three distinct agents: AI therapist (user-facing), AI supervisor (monitors dialogue and provides suggestions), and AI rater (evaluates belief changes); generative responses with supervisory oversight and guardrails to maintain focus and prevent inappropriate directions
quotes:
“Three distinct AI agents interact directly with one another to engage the user in Socratic dialogue. The user only interacts directly with an AI therapist.”
“an AI supervisor monitors the entire dialogue and provides the AI therapist with concrete suggestions for how to improve the Socratic dialogue”
“an AI rater evaluates changes in the users' belief as an indicator of possible progress and provides this information to the AI therapist so it can adjust the course of the intervention as needed.”
“The additional AI agents also help maintain focus and intervene if dialogues shift toward inappropriate or harmful directions.”
age_as_reported: at least aged 18 years; mean age 39.9 (SD 15.50) years

title: Breaking Barriers in Student Mental Health Care With AI-Enhanced Group Cognitive Behavioral Therapy: Pilot Feasibility Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: LLM (Claude 3.7-Sonnet) with deterministic system prompts embedding UP therapeutic principles guiding generative responses. System prompt customized per participant with conversation summaries. Human-in-the-loop safety with therapist review of shared/flagged conversations. Automatic flagging of self-harm or abuse mentions for human follow-up. Content constraints via UP-based system prompts.
quotes:
“The CBT ChatBot web application used Claude 3.7-Sonnet LLM, with system prompts explicitly embedding the core therapeutic principles of the UP.”
“The system prompt was further customized for each participant by including a concise summary of prior interactions to preserve conversational continuity.”
“the AI flagged any mention of self-harm or abuse for immediate human follow-up”
“In line with a "human-in-the-loop" safety principle, therapists could review both shared and flagged or inappropriate conversations”
loc: Methods, The Intervention Program and Chatbot Application; Discussion, Safety and Ethical Considerations
age_as_reported: university students aged 18 years and older; mean age 22.06, SD 1.78 years

title: Impact of Conversational and Animation Features of a Mental Health App Virtual Agent on Depressive Symptoms and User Experience Among College Students: randomized Controlled Trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: App built with Unity 2021; speech-to-text engine for user input; TTS engines (RTVoice Native for Android, Amazon Web Services Polly Standard for iOS) for agent dialogue. Conversational condition embedded question-and-response dialogue within CBT modules; nonconversational condition did not allow user input. Deterministic CBT module content with optional conversational interactivity.
quotes:
“Users initiated verbal input using a speech-to-text engine, the speech recognition system plugin, while audio-based agent dialogue was created using the following text-to-speech (TTS) engines: RTVoice Native for Android+ AmazonWeb Services Polly Standard for iOS.”
“The conversational feature was characterized by user-agent interactivity in whcih question-and-response style dialogue was embedded within the CBT modules.”
“The nonconversational condition did not allow the user to add their input or respond to questions.”
loc: Methods - AirHeart Mental Health App, p.4; Methods - Experimental Conditions, p.4-5
age_as_reported: 18-30 years; college students; mean age 19.97 years (SD 2.19)

title: Intelligent virtual agents in psychotherapy: a safety evaluation across high-risk mental health scenarios.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Model-orchestrated (generative). The system relied primarily on a single high-level instructional system prompt to GPT-4omni, with no additional rule-based safety filters, structured clinical decision trees, or automated risk-classification modules. The prompt was concise and principle-based rather than algorithmic. Model autonomy was high, with performance largely dependent on the LLM's internal training and interpretation of instructions.
quotes:
“the system relied primarily on this single high-level instructional prompt and did not include additional rule-based safety filters, structured clinical decision trees, or automated risk-classification modules operating in parallel”
“the agent's performance was largely dependent on the large language model's internal training and its interpretation of the provided instructions.”
“The prompt was intentionally concise and principle-based rather than algorithmic. It did not contain explicit stepwise suicide risk assessment procedures, structured diagnostic criteria, mandatory crisis-escalation scripts, or predefined response templates.”
age_as_reported: Testers: mean age 39 years (SD=9.90); Raters: mean age 32 years (SD=1.41). All licensed psychotherapists.

title: Evaluating Generative AI in Mental Health: Systematic Review of Capabilities and Limitations
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Generative LLM components (ChatGPT-3.5/4.0, Bard, Claude) with no described workflow orchestration. Most studies used zero-shot prompting (deterministic single input-output). One study used chain-of-thought prompting. No content constraints, guardrails, or model autonomy controls described.
quotes:
“The most used prompting method was zero-shot prompting (5 out of 8)”
“Chain-of-thought refers to the method where LLMs were provided with step-by-step reasoning examples rather than question-and-answer examples”

title: Therapy chatbots and emotional complexity: do therapy chatbots really empathise?. [Review]
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Both rule-based (deterministic) and generative (LLM) architectures discussed. Woebot and Wysa are rule-based using NLP without LLM integration; Youper has GenAI integrated. Rule-based systems described as more predictable, inflexible, and repetitive compared to LLM engines.
quotes:
“Woebot and Wysa are rule-based chatbots that make use of natural language processing (NLP) without LLM integration; other therapy chatbots, such as Youper, already have GenAI integrated”
“rule-based systems tend to generate more predictable, inflexible, and repetitive responses compared to advanced LLM engines”

title: Feasibility and User Experience of an AI-Supported mHealth Intervention for Remote Life Goal Setting Based on Flow Theory: Exploratory Within-Participant Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration: deterministic structure (fixed R-ACS steps, evaluation logic, persona) with generative content (dynamic feedback and goal adjustment suggestions generated by GPT-4o). System prompt governs behavior with fixed vs variable elements. Safety rules include prohibition of medical diagnoses/clinical advice, concealment of internal instructions, and privacy protection. Model autonomy limited to content of feedback and adjustment suggestions.
quotes:
“To ensure consistency and safety, the AI's behavior was governed by a strictly defined system prompt”
“The fixed elements included the intervention structure (R-ACS steps), the evaluation logic based on the person-environment-occupation model and flow theory, and the persona (supportive coach tone). The variable elements were limited to the specific content of feedback and goal adjustment suggestions, which the AI generated dynamically in response to each participant's unique inputs.”
“the AI was explicitly prohibited from providing medical diagnoses or clinical advice”
loc: Methods, AI-Supported mHealth Intervention section; Methods, Prompt Structure and Safety, p.4
age_as_reported: aged between 20 and 76 years

title: Optimizing personalized psychological well-being interventions through digital phenotyping: results from a randomized non-clinical trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture with workflow-orchestrated decision tree structure driving conversation branching based on participant answers. Deterministic components for branching, generative NLP components including intention identification, emotion and polarity classifiers. Clustering algorithm creates user profiles and content recommendation system ranks exercises by expected utility.
quotes:
“The interactions with the chatbot were based on a decision tree whose branching is driven by the participants' answers”
“The users' responses activate various natural language processing (NLP) models, including intention identification, emotion and polarity classifiers”
“A clustering algorithm created a user profile and content recommendation system to provide personalized exercises based on users' responses.”

title: Does the AI-driven chatbot work? Effectiveness of the Woebot app in reducing anxiety and depression in group counseling courses and student acceptance of technological aids. [References].
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Workflow-orchestrated with deterministic components - Woebot automatically detects users' conditions and provides relevant conversations based on cognitive-behavioral therapy concepts. Users described responses as 'rigid and standardized' with pre-developed dialogue responses based on real human interactions.
quotes:
“It automatically detects users' conditions and provides relevant conversations and a variety of resources”
“it automatically detects and responds based on cognitive-behavioral therapy concepts”
“Essentially, the dialogue responses provided by Woebot are based on those developed from real human interactions.”
“the Woebot chatbot felt very rigid and standardized.”
age_as_reported: average age of 26.12 years

title: Designing Personality-Adaptive Conversational Agents for Mental Health Care.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture. The expository instantiation describes: (1) a conversational user interface (CUI) for input/output; (2) a bot service for natural language processing and conversational design; (3) an application core containing general logic, accessing database and personality mining results; (4) a personality mining service using NLP/word embeddings (LIWC, word2vec, GloVe, IBM Watson Personality Insights) to infer user personality; (5) a database/knowledge base storing therapeutic methods, communication forms, and learned interactions. Suggested platforms: Google Dialogflow, IBM Watson Assistant, Amazon Lex, Wit.AI. The application determines social role, communication type, and anthropomorphism degree dynamically based on user personality.
quotes:
“The application is the core of the PACA and contains the general logic of the system. It accesses information from the knowledge base (database) and the information from the personality insight service to decide how to interact with the user.”
“The personality mining service is responsible for analyzing the user's messages and determining the personality traits of the user.”
“This functionality could be realized with services such as Google Dialogflow, IBM Watson Assistant, Amazon Lex, or Wit.AI.”
age_as_reported: between 23 and 71 years old, with an average age of 36 years

title: Factors influencing patient engagement in mental health chatbots: A thematic analysis of findings from a systematic review of reviews.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Both rule-based (deterministic) and machine learning-based (generative) response generation methods identified; unbounded chatbots noted as requiring careful supervision due to potential errors in natural language understanding or response generation.
quotes:
“The method used by the chatbot to generate responses, such as rule-based or machine learning-based, can inﬂuence the quality of user engagement.”
“using unbounded chatbots should be accompanied by careful supervision of patient and chatbot interactions, and of safety functions.”

title: Application of Synchronous Text-Based Dialogue Systems in Mental Health Interventions: Systematic Review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Mix of human-delivered and automated components. Chatbots and conversational agents mentioned; pre-developed reusable responses; NLP for generating text-based dialogue; automated concierge services for pre-assessment. Deterministic pre-developed responses and generative NLP approaches both noted.
quotes:
“they also successfully evaluated in their study the utilization of pre-developed responses that could be reused in conversation with different clients”
“the application of NLP to generate text-based dialogue”
“a conversational agent was trained to utilize principles of Method of Levels (MOL) therapy”
“7Cups (www.7cups.com) has introduced a "therapist bot" that greets users and carries out basic assessments”
age_as_reported: Participant ages ranged across the lifespan with 5 studies testing interventions in child or adolescents samples (S3, S5, S6, S8, and S10), 3 in adolescent or adults (S2, S4, and S14), and 5 studies focused exclusively on adults (S1, S7, S9, S11, and S12)

title: A Relational Agent Intervention for Adolescents Seeking Mental Health Treatment: outcomes From a Randomized Controlled Trial Within a Children's Outpatient Hospital
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: NLP algorithms process free-text entries combined with deterministic forced-choice button replies; safety net protocol uses NLP algorithm matching text against a priori word/phrase list to flag concerning language; clinician escalation triggered for crisis responses.
quotes:
“Conversations are supported by both natural language–processing algorithms at free-text entries as well as forced-choice button replies, with check-ins to conﬁrm understanding and motivation for next steps.”
“W-GenZD's “safety net protocol” was based on a natural language–processing algorithm designed to detect concerning language. The algorithm ﬂagged text input that may contain concerning language by matching it with an a priori list of words and phrases.”
age_as_reported: 13 to 17 years of age

title: SleepPathfinder: A Socratic Questioning and Self-Decision-Based Chatbot to Support User Engagement in Digital CBT-I: Usability and Feasibility Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid workflow and model orchestration; LLM-based dialogue generator with deterministic intent classifier; retrieval-augmented generation for advice provision; content constraints through clinical templates
quotes:
“dialogue generator that produces Socratic questions and empathic responses using a large language model (LLM)”
“intent classifier that maps user utterances to CBT-I techniques”
“retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach”
“clinically reviewed educational content based on established guidelines”
age_as_reported: Pilot: mean age 27.4, SD 8.5 years; Experimental: mean age 26.4, SD 3.7 years; undergraduate and graduate students

title: Therapeutic Interaction Features of AI Chatbots in Depression Interventions: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Three operational categories: (1) LLM-based — large pretrained generative models generating open-ended responses; (2) NLP/ML-based — intent classifiers, decision trees, response selection within constrained conversational flows; (3) Rule-based — fixed scripts or expert-crafted rules. The review distinguishes generative (LLM) from deterministic (rule-based) and hybrid (NLP/ML) approaches.
quotes:
“LLM-based chatbots as systems built on large pretrained generative models (eg, GPT, Gemini, and Claude) that directly generate responses in an open-ended way.”
“NLP-/ML-based chatbots are systems that use more traditional NLP or ML methods, such as intent classifiers, decision trees, or response selection within constrained conversational flows.”
“Rule-based chatbots are systems that rely on fixed scripts or expert-crafted rules.”
age_as_reported: Individuals with depression or depressive symptoms; ages range from mean ~18.78 to 41.4 years across included studies; some studies do not report age

title: Conversational Agents in Health Care: Scoping Review of Their Behavior Change Techniques and Underpinning Theory.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Rule-based algorithms used to design conversation flow, either alone (35/47, 75%) or complemented with AI (2/47, 4%). 9/47 (19%) were AI-based CAs using natural language processing or machine learning. 4/47 (9%) were hybrid rule-based + AI.
quotes:
“Most CAs used rule-based algorithms to design the flow of conversations, either by themselves (35/47, 75%) or complemented with AI (2/47, 4%)”
“CAs can be further classified as simple rule-based agents or smart, artificial intelligence (AI)–based agents using natural language processing or machine learning”
country: USA, GBR, JPN, KOR, CHE, AUS, FRA, DEU, IND, NLD, ESP, SWE

title: Mind Meets Machine: A Narrative Review of Artificial Intelligence Role in Clinical Psychology Practice. [Review]
label: Orchestration architecture
value: The review describes hybrid 'AI-in-the-loop' systems where AI supports assessment, triage, and monitoring while clinicians retain decision-making. Both deterministic (automated scoring) and generative (conversational agents) components are discussed. Human oversight and guardrails are emphasized.
quotes:
“hybrid 'AI-­in-­the-­loop' systems show promise in supporting engagement and personalization”
“AI-­driven applications are responsible for supporting the tasks of assessment, triage and monitoring, while the clinician concentrates their attention toward the classificatory and interpersonal dimensions”

title: An overview of the features of chatbots in mental health: A scoping review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Rule-based (deterministic decision trees) in 92.5% of studies; machine learning approaches in 7.5% of studies (1 supervised ML, 1 reinforcement learning). Rule-based chatbots have predetermined responses and restrict user input to predefined words/phrases.
quotes:
“In the majority of studies (92.5%), chatbots generated their responses based on some predefined rules or decision trees (rule-based).”
“rule-based chatbots are more simple to develop and less prone to errors as their responses are predetermined and they do not need to create new responses”
“rule-based chatbots cannot respond to users' inputs outside of the determined rules”
country: USA, JPN, AUS, NLD, FRA, GBR, TUR, DEU, SWE, GRC, ESP, KOR, PAK, CHN, MEX, ROU, SCO (multi-country review of included studies)
age_as_reported: Mean age of participants across 33 studies was 37.1 years; no specific age band restriction

title: Development of a Mobile Intervention for Procrastination Augmented With a Semigenerative Chatbot for University Students: pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration: predetermined scenario framework with generative model components. Two primary algorithms: (1) response-generating algorithm (answer classifier using Korean BERT classifies user responses as uncertain/skeptical/normal; answer generator using Korean GPT-2 fine-tuned for the scenario generates responses), and (2) procrastination factor algorithm (multilayered CNN classifier detecting 6 procrastination factors to provide tailored advice). Deterministic scenario flow with generative responses within each step. Content restricted to procrastination-related topics.
quotes:
“we designed a chatbot architecture comprising 2 primary algorithms: a response-generating and a procrastination factor algorithm”
“Moa includes generative models in a predetermined scenario based on the CBT process to encourage active user engagement in conversations while maintaining consistency to guide behavior change”
“we incorporated predetermined questionnaires and established a scenario to maintain context within a conversation”

title: Effectiveness and Safety of Using Chatbots to Improve Mental Health: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Rule-based (predefined rules/decision trees) in 8/12 studies; AI-based (machine learning and NLP) in 4/12. Chatbots led and controlled conversation in 9/12 (system-initiated). No details on content constraints or guardrails.
quotes:
“Chatbot responses were based on predefined rules or decision trees (rule-based) in two-thirds of studies (8/12).”
“Chatbots in the remaining one-third of studies (4/12) utilized machine learning and natural language processing (artificial intelligence) to understand users'replies and generate responses.”
“Chatbots led and controlled the conversation in 75% (9/12) of the studies.”
loc: Results, Description of Included Studies, p.7
country: Multiple countries - studies conducted in more than 11 countries
age_as_reported: mean age of participants in those studies was 31.3 years

title: Combining AI and human support in mental health: a digital intervention with comparable effectiveness to human-delivered care
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration: primarily tree-based (deterministic) dialogue system with controlled use of natural language generation in specific instances. AI models used for Natural Language Understanding, tailored elements of Natural Language Generation, and a dialogue management system. Not fully autonomous language generation due to safety concerns.
quotes:
“The software used AI models for Natural Language Understanding, specific and tailored elements of Natural Language Generation and a dialogue management system”
“the digital program primarily used a tree-based dialogue system with controlled use of natural language generation in specific instances to enhance engagement”
“allowing fully autonomous language generation within the context of mental health, where patient problems can be nuanced, complex and require the consideration of social and cultural contexts, poses a high risk for patient harm and misuse”
age_as_reported: over the age of 18 years at point of recruitment; mean age 39.8 years (range: 18 – 75 years)

title: Is This Chatbot Safe and Evidence-Based? A Call for the Critical Evaluation of Generative AI Mental Health Chatbots.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Model-orchestrated; generative components; guided by system prompt instructions
quotes: “GenAI chatbots, in contrast, are driven by powerful large language models (LLMs) that produce customized responses to each user message, guided by the instructions written in the "system prompt" provided to the LLM”

title: Applications of artificial intelligence-based conversational agents in healthcare: A systematic umbrella review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Most AI-based CAs developed using Deep Learning methods (n=14), used independently or combined with NLP (n=12), NLU (n=5), or NLG (n=2). Across included reviews, chatbot types include rule-based, retrieval-based, AI-based, and hybrid. Generative AI (GPT, BERT, LSTM) reported in some reviews. Development platforms include RASA, DialogFlow, IBM Watson, Amazon Lex, among others.
quotes:
“Most AI-based CAs were developed using deep Learning methods (n = 14). These deep Learning techniques were used independent from or in combination with Natural Language Processing (n = 12), Natural Language Understanding (n = 5), or Natural Language Generation (n = 2).”
“Type: AI (n = 20), rule-based (n = 8), hybrid (n = 5)”
“Chatbot development platforms: RASA, Botsify, Chatfuel, Manychat, FlowXO, Chatterbot, Pandorabot, Botkit, Botlytics, NLU cloud platforms such as Google DialogFlow, Facebook wit.ai, Microsoft LUIS, IMB Watson Conversation, Amazon Lex, SAP Conversation AI.”

title: Our journey with an AI assistant offering narrative therapy on WhatsApp. [References].
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid orchestration: deterministic stepwise instructions (25-step procedure) guide the conversational flow through 5 NT stages, while generative GPT-4 model produces responses. The AI has conditional actions for different user responses and example utterances to guide language. Content constraints include: responses under 100 words, no clinical advice, inductive observations only, communication only in English or traditional Chinese, and referral to professional counselling if user is distressed.
quotes:
“We set up the AI assistant using OpenAI's Assistant API, which is the system endpoint of ChatGPT (https://platform.openai.com/) using its GPT-4 model.”
“What began as a simple framework evolved into a more complex, 25-step set of instructions.”
“Be friendly and supportive, but keep your responses brief, under 100 words.”
“You do not provide clinical advice or suggestions directly, you make inductive observations and encourage users to think about those observations.”
“If a user is distressed by their memories, gently suggest they seek professional counselling.”

title: Agents of change: Understanding the therapeutic processes associated with the helpfulness of therapy for mental health problems with relational agent MYLO.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Deterministic/workflow-orchestrated approach: analyses free-text input for key terms, phrases, and themes, then responds with pre-set questions aimed at encouraging higher-level awareness. No generative components described.
quotes:
“Users type free-text about their problem and MYLO analyses text input for key terms, phrases, and themes”
“MYLO responds with questions aimed at encouraging higher-level awareness of a problem”
age_as_reported: aged 16 and over; actual sample mean 33.4 years (SD 14.5), range 22–67

title: Generative AI-Powered Mental Wellness Chatbot for College Student Mental Wellness: Open Trial
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: generative AI-powered chatbot with structured single-session intervention format. Deterministic structure (concern identification, goal setting, tool selection, practice, action plan, summary) with generative AI producing dynamic, context-aware responses. Safety guardrails include crisis detection and rerouting, SOS button linking to 988 and Crisis Text Line.
quotes:
“Unlike scripted chatbots, Wayhaven dynamically adapts to users' real-time needs while ensuring safety through advanced crisis detection and rerouting”
“Conversations follow a structured single-session intervention format”
age_as_reported: college students aged 18 years or older; mean age 22.12 (SD 4.42) years

title: Integrating ChatGPT: Enhancing postpartum mental healthcare with artificial intelligence (AI) support.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid model proposed where AI supports but does not replace human therapists. ChatGPT (generative LLM) used as supplementary tool. No technical orchestration architecture, guardrails, or content constraints described.
quotes: “A hybrid model, where AI supports but does not replace human therapists, could strike the right balance”

title: Use of automated conversational agents in improving young population mental health: a scoping review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Almost half of automated CAs (n = 12) employed natural language processing and machine learning to carry on an interaction. Predeﬁned dialog or interactions assembled, and matched to the user input in a dynamic manner was used in 10 studies, while 3 used a mixed dialog system.
quotes:
“almost half of automated CAs (n = 12) employed natural language processing and machine learning to carry on an interaction8,9,12,27,30,31,34,38,39,41,43,45”
“Predeﬁned dialog or interactions assembled, and matched to the user input in a dynamic manner was used in 10 studies10,11,26,28,29,32,33,35,40,44, while 3 used a mixed dialog system36,37,42”

title: ChatGPT Clinical Use in Mental Health Care: Scoping Review of Empirical Evidence.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Primarily generative (LLM-based) with no explicit orchestration architecture described. Studies used standard ChatGPT, custom instruction GPT, or customized GPT models. Prompting techniques included zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting. Fine-tuned models consistently outperformed standard versions. No explicit guardrails or content constraints described at review level.
quotes:
“most studies employed standard ChatGPT (n=50)”
“Customized ChatGPTs were used in 6 studies [18,36,47,49,54,71], while 4 studies employed a custom instruction GPT model [10,63,74,75]”
“adding more examples in the prompt on how to carry out the detection tasks enhances the ChatGPT detection capabilities compared to zero-shot prompting condition”
“use of the chain-of-thought technique improves diagnostic accuracy, since the model is encouraged to reason step-by-step”
loc: Results, Characteristics of Clinical Applications, p.5; Discussion, Factors Accounting for Performance Variability, p.8
age_as_reported: adults (n=56), children and adolescents (n=4)

title: Chatbots to support young adults' mental health: An exploratory study of acceptability. [References].
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Workflow-orchestrated using Motion.ai development kit, deterministic conversation paths based on user input. No generative/model-orchestrated components described.
quotes:
“The chatbot was developed using the Motion.ai development kit”
“The user input, in the form of either clickable responses or natural language, determines the "path" of the conversation with the chatbot.”
age_as_reported: Ninety percent were aged between 18 and 20 (41%) and 21–24 (49%), with 10% aged 25 years or older

title: Designing conversational intelligence: effect of large language models (GPT-driven) platforms for precision maternal and newborn health engagement: a systematic review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Heterogeneous architectures across studies: hybrid approaches combining rule-based reliability with LLM/GPT adaptability are highlighted as most promising. Systems include AIML/Pandorabots (rule-based), Rasa open-source platform with NLP/ML (Juno), Random Forest with NLP (PregBot), decision tree with forward chaining (Puspitasari), deep learning models ANN/LSTM/BiLSTM/GRU/BiGRU (GyBot), GPT-4 (ChatGPT-4), and DialogFlow API. Both deterministic (rule-based, predefined Q&A) and generative (GPT-2) components described. Human oversight and predefined vetted content recommended as guardrails.
quotes:
“Hybrid approaches: integrating rule-based reliability with LLM/GPT adaptability appear most promising.”
“This model leverages LLM/GPT analytical power while minimizing risks via predefined, vetted content and human oversight.”
“The rule-based model performed best overall, providing human-like, content-speciﬁc and empathetic responses. The generative model was seen as engaging but often produced confusing or nonsensical replies.”
country: Multi-country (12 countries across included studies; review conducted from Iran)
age_as_reported: Pregnant and postpartum women (and partners); one study included women aged 18–40

title: The Digital Therapeutic Alliance With Mental Health Chatbots: Diary Study and Thematic Analysis.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Both chatbots operated mainly with predefined decision pathways and natural-language classifiers, rather than open-ended generative AI. Deterministic/rule-based components. Woebot uses structured conversation flow with predefined reply options. Wysa uses free-text input with natural-language classifiers. No generative AI components at time of study.
quotes: “both Woebot and Wysa operated mainly with predefined decision pathways and natural-language classifiers, rather than open-ended generative AI”
age_as_reported: aged 17 to 35 years (mean age 23, SD 4.66 y)

title: Empowering pediatric, adolescent, and young adult patients with cancer utilizing generative AI chatbots to reduce psychological burden and enhance treatment engagement: a pilot study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Model-orchestrated (generative) with deterministic safety guardrails. GPT-4 LLM generates responses via prompt engineering. Automated escalation systems detect critical keywords/suicidal ideation and provide crisis referral. Token-limit constraint restricts sessions to four exchanges. Content constrained by detailed system prompts specifying persona, tone, and conversational rules.
quotes:
“These design principles were implemented using prompt engineering techniques speciﬁc to the large language model [GPT-4 (12)] employed in this study.”
“Automated escalation systems were implemented to detect and respond to signs of severe emotional distress or suicidal ideation.”
“we restricted each conversation session to four consecutive user–chatbot exchanges.”
age_as_reported: pediatric and adolescent/young adult (AYA) cancer patients

title: Current Landscape and Future Directions for Mental Health Conversational Agents for Youth: Scoping Review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: NLP (19/39, 49%) used to process free-textual input, while rule-based programming (15/39, 38%) delivered prewritten content. CAs used multiple AI techniques depending on the specific section or feature. NLP determined routing to subsequent conversational nodes; rule-based methods triggered prewritten responses. None used generative AI or LLMs. Some CAs relied solely on decision trees or rule-based programs with no free-text capability.
quotes:
“Many CAs Used Multiple AI Techniques: Free-Textual Inputs Were Processed via Natural Language Processing, While Prewritten Content Was Delivered via Rule-Based Programming”
“Mostly, the CAs deliver prewritten conversational lessons via rule-based programming. However, they use techniques such as NLP at certain points in the tree to determine routing to subsequent conversational nodes”
“None of the mental health CAs we reviewed were built upon generative AI such as large language models (LLMs).”
country: USA, NZL, AUS, GBR, CHN, BRA, DEU, ITA, NOR, ARG, BGD, BEL, CAN, NLD, PHL, PRT
age_as_reported: youth aged between 15 and 24 years (UN definition); included studies cover adolescents (12-18), young adults (18-30), and youth (14-25)

title: Conversational Agent Interventions for Mental Health Problems: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
label: Orchestration architecture
value: CAs equipped with computer models ranging from deterministic decision trees with predefined responses to machine learning-based and natural language processing algorithms that classify real-time multimodal input into emotional states for empathic responses. Most CAs provide automated services without human participation.
quotes:
“CAs are equipped with computer models that range from succinct decision trees, where different responses to a questionnaire result in different responses from the CAs to machine learning–based and natural language processing–based algorithms that classify real-time multimodal input into a user's emotional state, allowing the CAs to respond empathically”
“most CAs for mental health issues can independently provide automated services to users without the participation and guidance of human”
country: USA, GBR, SWE, JPN, KOR, CHE, CAN, ARG, CHN, IRL, NLD, DEU, NZL
age_as_reported: The average age was 36.32 (SD 13.44; range 21.40-71.47) years

title: RACares: a conceptual design to guide mHealth relational agent development based on a systematic review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture with five-stage workflow (input receiving → processing → analysis → output processing → output generation) and Data and Personalization Controller. Predominantly deterministic rule-based dialogue management (24/29 RAs), with 2 using probabilistic decision trees. Content manually created by designers with domain expert assistance.
quotes:
“Among the 29 RAs, 24 utilized a deterministic, rule-based strategy to manage conversations, while 2 used a probabilistic decision tree approach”
“The dialogue was manually created by designers with the assistance of domain experts and existing theories for specific healthcare contexts”
“The conceptual design has five independent stages with one supporting module and one data controller”
“This stage may make use of a single or several rule-based, machine learning (ML)-based, or keyword matching-based content production techniques”
loc: Results, p.7; Proposed conceptual design, p.7-11

title: Artificial intelligence in perinatal mental health research: A scoping review.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Mixed architectures across studies: rule-based NLP tool with five layers of linguistic processing [74]; supervised ML chatbot using SVM with RBF kernel [76]; Tess AI system adapted for automated psychological support [45] (algorithms undisclosed); voice assistants using existing commercial NLP [46]. Deterministic rule-based components in [74]; generative/ML components in [76].
quotes:
“A rule-based NLP tool consisting of five layers of linguistic processing was developed in a study.”
“Tess AI system adapted for automated psychological support”
“Another study designed a chatbot architecture to monitor and assess the mental state of perinatal women, in which ML models were trained to classify perinatal women”

title: A LLM-Based Chatbot for Mindfulness Practice with Older Adults: A Development and Usability Study.
label: Orchestration architecture
value: Hybrid architecture: fine-tuned OpenAI GPT-4 (generative LLM) with hallucination control via prompt tuning and retrieval-augmented generation
quotes:
“a prototype LLM-based mindfulness coach was developed by fine-tuning OpenAI's GPT-4 on a custom dataset of Swedish mindfulness scripts”

value: Four distinct personas (woman in 30s with relationship problems, retired man with chronic pain, teenage boy with bullying, woman grieving loss). Two prompt strategy dimensions varied: concreteness (personal story-driven vs clinical assessment-driven) and resistance (reserved/hostile vs open/amicable). Response length adapted (1-2 sentences for reserved/hostile condition). VPs instructed to withhold certain topics until later in conversation. No language-register adaptation or memory across sessions described.
quotes:
“These four included: (1) a woman in her 30's going through problems with her girlfriend; (2) a retired man dealing with chronic pain and loneliness; (3) a teenage boy struggling with bullying and questioning his sexuality; and (4) a woman grieving the loss of a loved one.”
“Your responses should usually be about 1-2 sentences”
“Don't say this immediately”
age_as_reported: Participants were 18 or older; child welfare data concerns children referred to CYF. No specific youth age band targeted for mental health interventions.

title: Co-design and evaluation of a smartphone-based mental health promotion and anti-stigma embodied conversational agent for church-affiliated Black adults.
label: Personalisation features
value: Tailoring by user type (PwD vs CM), stigma status, mental health status (PHQ-8 scores), and cultural/spiritual preferences. Surface-structure tailoring (agent appearance as African American woman) and deep-structure tailoring (Scripture, culturally-relevant health content, racial/ethnic barriers to care). Seven unique faith-based 'getting to know you' scripts. Symptom check-ins tailored to most severe reported PHQ-8 symptom. Resources tailored by user type. However, spiritual tailoring used a one-size-fits-all approach rather than adaptive.

“the implementation of the cultural and spiritual tailoring used a one-size-fits-all approach”

title: The Efficacy of Rule-Based Versus Large Language Model-Based Chatbots in Alleviating Symptoms of Depression and Anxiety: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
label: Personalisation features
value: Rule-based chatbots lack personalization, relying on predefined keywords. LLM-based chatbots can adjust intervention processes and depth based on user expressions, continuously optimize response strategies based on dialogue history, and dynamically adjust conversational strategies, tone, and content depth based on real-time emotional state, cognitive level, and language expression habits.
quotes:
“these chatbots lack the ability to provide personalized responses and rely on predefined keywords to trigger crisis intervention processes”
“They can adjust intervention processes and depth based on user expressions”
“Their core advantage lies in personalized algorithms that can intelligently identify crisis risks and continuously optimize response strategies based on dialogue history”
“LLM can dynamically adjust conversational strategies, tone, and content depth based on the user's real-time emotional state, cognitive level, and language expression habits”
loc: Results, Component Analysis, Treatment Components, p.13; Discussion, Optimization Phase, p.16
country: USA, CHN (67% combined); other countries not fully enumerated

title: What should be included in a digital mental health intervention, based on solution-focused therapy, for young people who self-harm? A qualitative exploration of young people and clinicians' views.

Participants wanted clear, straightforward messages based in reality rather than too abstract. Tone preferences varied — some wanting professional, others friend-like. The 'best hopes' question preferred as opening. Scaling questions used to measure progress. Relationship questions for perspective-taking.

title: The Effectiveness and Feasibility of Conversational Agents in Supporting Care for Patients With Cancer: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

title: Chatbots and Conversational Agents in Mental Health: A Review of the Psychiatric Landscape.
